original_metadata.title: Cyclic-module identification for homogeneous quotient-coalgebra Galois extensions of Hopf algebras with invertible antipode and adjoint coefficients
original_metadata.author: Tomasz Maszczyk; Serkan Sutlu
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs inverse maps between relative cyclic chains and Hopf-cyclic chains for quotient coalgebras that need not be Hopf algebras. Well-definedness requires both balancing relations and the adjoint-coefficient identities, and the author separately verifies inverse composition, all faces, degeneracies and the cyclic operator.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Complete Lemma3.3 inverse-chain construction and Theorem3.4 proof read. H is a Hopf algebra over the standing field k with the invertible antipode used in Section2.4; I is a coideal right ideal and B=H coinvariants for H/I is an H/I-Galois extension. Adjoint coefficients are exactly the action(3.4) and coproduct coaction specified immediately before Lemma3.3. Prior Takeuchi/Galois identities I=B-plus H and the translation map are cited background; no requirement that H/I itself have a Hopf-algebra structure is added. The spectral sequence, Pontryagin dual theorem and classical orbit applications are excluded.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem3.4 with its explicit mutually inverse maps(3.6)-(3.7): relative cyclic module of B subset H, B=H co(H/I), is isomorphic to the H-balanced cyclic module of H/I with the specified adjoint SAYD coefficients. Standing invertibility of the antipode, coideal-right-ideal I and homogeneous H/I-Galois condition retained.
original_metadata.editorial_warning: Theorem3.4 reverses the prose handedness of the adjoint action/coaction relative to the explicit preceding formula(3.4) and tensor-balanced module construction; the selected coefficients are fixed by those formulas. The cyclic-operator verification writes phi_(n+1) once where its displayed domain has n+1 factors and the surrounding map is phi_n. Original author bytes remain unchanged.
original_metadata.source_boundary_note: Full original Theorem 3.4, the complete Lemma 3.3 mutually inverse chain construction and all required quotient-coalgebra Galois, adjoint-coefficient and cyclic-module definitions are retained. The H/I quotient is not assumed to be a Hopf algebra; the standing invertible antipode, coideal right ideal and homogeneous Galois hypotheses are preserved. The new balancing, inverse-composition, face, degeneracy and cyclic-operator computations form one author-positioned main problem unit. Prior Takeuchi/Galois correspondences and translation identities remain cited established prerequisites. No spectral sequence, duality theorem or orbit application is separately selected.
